name: io_register_resize_rings
prose: Precondition: ctx is an io_ring_ctx and arg is a user pointer to a struct io_uring_params; the caller is expected to hold ctx->uring_lock (the function drops and retakes it only around io_sq_thread_park when ctx->sq_data is set). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno. Early returns before any lock beyond uring_lock: -EINVAL if IORING_SETUP_DEFER_TASKRUN is not set in ctx->flags or if p.flags has bits outside RESIZE_FLAGS; -EFAULT if copy_from_user fails; the return of io_uring_fill_params if nonzero; -EOVERFLOW if rings_size() or the later SQE array_size() returns SIZE_MAX. It allocates a new ring region (io_create_region_mmap_safe, IORING_OFF_CQ_RING), writes the new masks/entries into the new rings, copies p back to userspace (-EFAULT on failure) and allocates a new SQE region; each of these failures frees the new rings via io_register_free_rings and returns without touching ctx->rings. It then parks the SQPOLL thread if ctx->sq_data, takes ctx->mmap_lock and ctx->completion_lock, and moves the old rings and SQEs into o with ctx->rings and ctx->sq_sqes set to NULL. It copies the pending SQEs (head..tail) and CQEs into the new regions; if the pending SQ count exceeds p.sq_entries, the pending CQ count exceeds p.cq_entries, or on a CQE_MIXED ring a 32-byte CQE would land on the last destination slot, it restores ctx->rings and ctx->sq_sqes from o, frees the new rings and returns -EOVERFLOW. On success it copies sq_dropped, sq_flags, cq_flags and cq_overflow, sets ctx->sq_array only when IORING_SETUP_NO_SQARRAY is clear, sets ctx->sq_entries and cq_entries, sets IORING_SQ_TASKRUN and IORING_SQ_NEED_WAKEUP in the new sq_flags, publishes the new rings (ctx->rings and ctx->rings_rcu) and SQEs, swaps the region descriptors with swap_old, and returns 0 after releasing both locks, calling synchronize_rcu_expedited, freeing the old rings and unparking the SQPOLL thread if one was parked.
note: slice cut the head; read whole function io_uring/register.c:402-. Reviewer (sq_array only updated when NO_SQARRAY clear) is right: line 590. Full prose rewritten.

name: io_validate_user_buf_range
prose: Precondition: uaddr is a user address and ulen a length, both u64. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if ulen is zero or greater than SZ_1G; otherwise computes acct_len as PAGE_ALIGN(ulen) and base as uaddr, both converted to unsigned long, and returns -EOVERFLOW if base + acct_len overflows unsigned long (check_add_overflow); otherwise returns 0. It reads no global state and does not check that the range is mapped or accessible.
note: reviewer (contract omits user precondition, assumes 64-bit) right; contract left empty. rsrc.c:84-95. The u64-to-unsigned long casts truncate on 32-bit builds.

name: __io_read
prose: Precondition: req is an io_uring read request, sel is the buffer-selection state, issue_flags carries IO_URING_F_NONBLOCK and IO_URING_F_MULTISHOT bits; req->async_data holds the iterator state. Postcondition: returns a ssize_t-valued int, which is a negative errno, IOU_ISSUE_SKIP_COMPLETE, or a byte count from the last read attempt only. Early returns: the nonzero result of io_rw_import_reg_vec when REQ_F_IMPORT_BUFFER is set; a negative result of io_import_rw_buffer when buffer select is used; the nonzero result of io_rw_init_file; -EAGAIN when issue_flags has IO_URING_F_NONBLOCK and the file does not support nowait; the nonzero result of rw_verify_area. It then sets req->cqe.res to the iterator count, sets or clears IOCB_NOWAIT, and calls io_iter_do_read; -EOPNOTSUPP is converted to -EAGAIN when nonblocking. On -EAGAIN it returns -EAGAIN if the file can poll; goes to done (returning -EAGAIN) if it is blocking without IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL, or if REQ_F_NOWAIT is set; otherwise sets ret to 0 and enters the retry loop. On -EIOCBQUEUED it returns IOU_ISSUE_SKIP_COMPLETE. It goes straight to done and returns that result if the read returned the full requested count, returned 0 or a negative value, is not nonblocking, has REQ_F_NOWAIT, does not need need_complete_io, or is multishot. Otherwise (partial read or the retry case) it restores the iterator and loops: advance the iterator by ret; if no bytes remain, leave the loop (returning that last ret); else add ret to io->bytes_done and save state; if io_rw_should_retry is false, clear IOCB_WAITQ and return -EAGAIN; otherwise reissue the read with io_iter_do_read, returning IOU_ISSUE_SKIP_COMPLETE on -EIOCBQUEUED, and repeat while the read returns a positive count. The loop ends returning the final ret (0, a negative errno, or the last chunk). The returned positive value does not include io->bytes_done accumulated by earlier iterations.
note: reviewer right: the return on a partial retry is only the last chunk, bytes_done is added only in the loop (rw.c:997,1022). The earlier 'iterator restored not advanced' claim is covered by the loop at 985-994.

name: bpf_prog2
prose: Tracepoint program for power/cpu_frequency (SEC "tracepoint/power/cpu_frequency"); ctx supplies the new state (frequency) and cpu_id. Returns int; every return in the code returns 0. It looks up three entries of my_map for this cpu (pstate-time, pstate-idx, cstate-idx) and returns 0 if any lookup fails. It then stores ctx->state into the pstate-idx entry. If the stored timestamp *pts is zero it sets it to bpf_ktime_get_ns() and returns 0. Otherwise it computes delta = now - *pts, stores now in *pts, and returns 0 if *cstate is not (u32)-1 (CPU idle). Otherwise it computes pstate_idx = find_cpu_pstate_idx(*pstate) (the value just stored from ctx->state) and returns 0 if it is at least MAX_PSTATE_ENTRIES; else it looks up pstate_duration at key cpu * MAX_PSTATE_ENTRIES + pstate_idx and, if the lookup finds an element, atomically adds delta to it (__sync_fetch_and_add), then returns 0.
note: Listed name update_pstate_duration is not a function in the file; the slice (samples/bpf/cpustat_kern.c:271-280) is the tail of bpf_prog2 (lines 211-277), so fixed under the real name. Tool-driven, no reviewer claim beyond the name.

name: BPF_PROG(tp_xdp_devmap_xmit_multi, const struct net_device *from_dev, const struct net_device *to_dev, int sent, int drops, int err)
prose: BPF tracepoint program (macro-generated function tp_xdp_devmap_xmit_multi) attached to tp_btf/xdp_devmap_xmit; arguments are the source and destination net_device pointers and the sent, drops and err values. It builds idx = (from_dev->ifindex << 32) | to_dev->ifindex and returns 0 without recording if either ifindex fails the IN_SET filter (from_match, to_match). Otherwise it calls bpf_map_update_elem on devmap_xmit_cnt_multi with an empty datarec and BPF_NOEXIST (so an existing entry is not overwritten; the update's result is not checked), looks the entry up, and returns 0 if the lookup gives no element. If found it adds sent to rec->processed and drops to rec->dropped with non-tearing read/write-once adds, increments rec->info, and increments rec->issue if err is nonzero or drops is negative. Every return in the function returns 0.
note: Previously dropped as <unnamed>; slice (xdp_sample.bpf.c:255-266) is the tail of tp_xdp_devmap_xmit_multi (lines 236-266), so fixed rather than dropped.

name: damon_sample_prcl_init
prose: Module init function taking no arguments. If damon_initialized() is false it sets the module variable enabled to false when it was true and returns -ENOMEM. Otherwise, if enabled is true it calls damon_sample_prcl_start(); if that returns nonzero it sets enabled to false. In that second branch the function returns 0 whether or not the start call failed (its error value is only used to clear enabled). With enabled false and damon already initialised it does nothing and returns 0.
note: samples/damon/prcl.c:158-174. Reviewer only flagged contract omitting ENOMEM (mechanical); contract left empty because the function touches module globals. Counted as right.

name: kmemleak_test_init
prose: Module init function taking no arguments. It logs a message, then calls kmalloc eight times (two each of 32, 1024, 2048 and 4096 bytes), kmem_cache_alloc(files_cachep) twice only when CONFIG_MODULES is not defined, and vmalloc(64) five times; the returned pointers are only printed and are not stored, so those objects are left leaked by design. It then loops ten times: each iteration does kzalloc of a struct test_node, and on a NULL result returns -ENOMEM at once (objects allocated earlier are not freed); otherwise it initialises elem->list and adds it to the global test_list. Then for each possible CPU it stores a kmalloc(129) result in the per-CPU kmemleak_test_pointer (not checked for NULL), and it calls __alloc_percpu(64, 4) discarding the result, and returns 0. The only error return is -ENOMEM from the kzalloc loop.
note: kmemleak-test.c:35-85. Reviewer (contract constrains only return value, omits side effects) right; contract left empty.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the Nitro Enclaves sample; takes the enclave image path as argv[1]. It never returns: every path ends in exit(). It exits with EXIT_FAILURE if argc is not 2, if strlen(argv[1]) is at least PATH_MAX, if opening the NE device fails, or if ne_create_vm returns a negative value (the device fd is closed right after ne_create_vm either way). It then starts a thread running ne_poll_enclave_fd on the enclave fd; the test for failure is rc < 0, but pthread_create reports failure with a positive error number, so a failed thread creation is not caught by this check and the function continues. It allocates NE_DEFAULT_NR_MEM_REGIONS user memory regions of NE_MIN_MEM_REGION_SIZE each, loads the enclave image, registers each memory region, adds NE_DEFAULT_NR_VCPUS vCPUs (vcpu id 0 meaning pick from the pool) and calls ne_start_enclave_check_booted; a negative result from any of these jumps to release_enclave_fd, which closes the enclave fd, frees the memory regions and exits with EXIT_FAILURE. On success it sleeps NE_SLEEP_TIME seconds, closes the enclave fd, frees the regions and exits with EXIT_SUCCESS. The polling thread is not joined or cancelled by main.
note: slice cut the head; real function ne_ioctl_sample.c:766-882. Reviewer is right: pthread_create returns a positive errno value on failure, so rc < 0 (line 808) never detects failure (the old prose claimed that path).

name: user_trap_syscall
prose: Precondition: nr is a syscall number and flags are seccomp(2) filter flags (for example SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER). It builds a four-instruction classic BPF filter on the stack that loads the syscall number from struct seccomp_data and returns SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF when it equals nr and SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW otherwise, and returns the result of seccomp(SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER, flags, &prog) unchanged. On failure that is the seccomp wrapper's failure value (negative or -1 with errno set by the underlying call); on success it is 0, or, when flags include SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER, the new listener file descriptor. The function does not check the arguments itself.
note: user-trap.c:90-106. Original reviewer claim that fd is returned only with NEW_LISTENER was valid; current reviewer about contract is right; contract left empty (return depends on syscall).

name: TRACE_EVENT(foo_bar,
prose: Macro invocation, not a hand-written function: TRACE_EVENT(foo_bar, ...) declares the tracepoint foo_bar and generates its probe, assign and print code. The tracepoint takes foo (string), bar (int), lst (int list), string, mask (cpumask), fmt and va (a va_list pointer). Its ring-buffer entry has a 10-char array foo, an int bar, a dynamic int array list sized __length_of(lst) (0 for a NULL list, otherwise the count before the first 0 element), a string str, a bitmask cpus sized num_possible_cpus(), a cpumask cpum, a formatted string vstr from fmt and va, and a string lstr whose length is bar / 2 or strlen(foo), whichever comparison result selects (the comparison is between an int and a size_t). The assign step copies foo with strscpy into the 10-byte array, stores bar, memcpy's lst into the dynamic array using __length_of(lst) elements, assigns str, lstr and vstr, and copies the bitmask and cpumask from cpumask_bits(mask). The TP_printk format prints foo, bar, bar as a symbolic name (zero, TWO, FOUR, EIGHT, TEN), bar as a flag string, the list twice, str, lstr, the bitmask, cpumask, vstr, and the cpus bitmask with its length. It does not call any reg or unreg function.
note: trace-events-sample.h:291-378. Reviewer is right that the old prose omitted the lstr __string_len copy (line 307, 316). Kept as macro invocation per rule 5; no control flow of its own is visible, expansion not read.

name: TRACE_EVENT_FN(foo_bar_with_fn,
prose: Macro invocation, not a hand-written function: TRACE_EVENT_FN(foo_bar_with_fn, ...) declares the tracepoint foo_bar_with_fn with the arguments foo (const char *) and bar (int). Its entry holds the string foo and the int bar; the assign step stores the string with __assign_str and sets bar; the print format is "foo %s %d" with the string and bar. The last two arguments name foo_bar_reg and foo_bar_unreg, which the tracepoint core is documented (comment in the header) to call before the tracepoint is enabled and after it is disabled; the event's assign/probe code itself does not call them.
note: trace-events-sample.h:460-479. Reviewer right: reg/unreg are passed as TRACE_EVENT_FN parameters and are not called by the probe body.

name: mbochs_dev_init
prose: Module init function taking no arguments; returns 0 on success or the error value of the step that failed. It sets mbochs_avail_mbytes to max_mbytes, then calls alloc_chrdev_region for MINORMASK + 1 minors and returns its negative result immediately on failure (nothing to undo yet). It then calls cdev_init and cdev_add (the cdev_add result is not checked) and logs the major number. Each later failure unwinds only the steps below it: mdev_register_driver failing jumps to err_cdev (cdev_del and unregister_chrdev_region, without mdev_unregister_driver); class_register failing jumps to err_driver (mdev_unregister_driver, then cdev_del and unregister_chrdev_region); device_register failing jumps to err_put (put_device, class_unregister, then the err_driver steps; device_del is not called); mdev_register_parent failing jumps to err_device (device_del, then put_device, class_unregister and the err_driver steps). On failure it returns the saved ret. On success all registrations stay in place and it returns 0.
note: mbochs.c:1409-1458; slice cut the head. Reviewer is right (device_register failure skips device_del, mdev_register_driver failure skips mdev_unregister_driver) and an earlier reviewer was right that cdev_add's return is ignored (line 1421).

name: mbochs_check_framebuffer
prose: Precondition: mdev_state and mode are valid pointers; mdev_state->vbe holds the emulated Bochs dispi registers and the caller is expected to hold mdev_state->ops_lock (the function only issues WARN_ON(!mutex_is_locked(...)) and never takes or drops the lock). Postcondition: returns 0 and fills *mode (drm_format DRM_FORMAT_XRGB8888, bytepp 4, width = XRES register, height = YRES register, stride = max(VIRT_WIDTH, width) * 4, size = stride * height, offset = X_OFFSET * 4 + Y_OFFSET * stride, the last two computed in u64) only when the ENABLE register has VBE_DISPI_ENABLED, the BPP register is 32, width and height are both at least 64, and offset + size does not exceed mdev_state->memsize. In each other case (not enabled, bpp other than 32, width or height under 64, or offset + size above memsize) it zeroes *mode with memset and returns -EINVAL; the three rejections after the enable check also emit a rate-limited dev_info message.
note: Listed name mbochs_get_mode does not exist; the slice (mbochs.c:257-511) contains the body of mbochs_check_framebuffer (lines 250-300), so fixed under its real name.

name: render_out_of_line_list
prose: Precondition: out is the output FILE; the global queue render_list holds elements queued for out-of-line rendering. Returns nothing. While render_list is non-empty it removes the head element e (resetting render_list_p to &render_list when the queue becomes empty), writes a newline with render_more, records e->entry_index as the current nr_entries, and renders each child of e with render_element at render_depth + 1. Children that are queued while rendering are processed by later iterations of the same loop. It then emits the closing opcodes based on e->compound: SEQUENCE emits ASN1_OP_END_SEQ, SEQUENCE_OF emits ASN1_OP_END_SEQ_OF followed by _jump_target(entry), SET emits ASN1_OP_END_SET, SET_OF emits ASN1_OP_END_SET_OF followed by _jump_target(entry), where entry is the nr_entries value recorded before the children were rendered; the END opcodes carry the _ACT suffix when e->action is set; any other compound value emits no end opcode. Independent of the compound, if e->action is set it emits _action(ACT_<name>), and always finally ASN1_OP_RETURN. The loop ends when the queue is empty.
note: asn1_compiler.c:1392-1434. Reviewer right: the old prose omitted the _jump_target(entry) emitted after the SEQUENCE_OF/SET_OF end opcodes (lines 1417, 1424).

name: main
prose: Entry point of the dtc compiler; reads options with util_getopt_long, then converts one input file. It does not return from the end of the loop: the last statement is exit(0), and error paths end in die() or usage() (reported by their names; their exit behaviour is not in this file). Options: -I/-O input and output format, -o output name (default "-"), -V output version, -d dependency file, -R/-S/-p/-a numeric sizes (-a must be a power of 2, else die), -f force, -q quiet, -b boot cpuid, -i search path, -H phandle format (legacy, epapr or both, else die), -s sort, -W/-E check options, -@, -L, -A, -T flags, -v and -h. After options, more than one positional argument calls usage("missing files"); no positional means "-" (stdin); setting both -S and -p dies. With -d it opens the dependency file for writing (die on failure) and prints the escaped output name plus ':'. It then picks the input format (guessed from the file name when -I is not given) and the output format (from the name if not given, else dtb for dts input or dts otherwise); --annotate requires dts in and dts out. It builds the tree from source, fs or blob input (anything else dies), closes the dependency file after adding a newline, sets the boot cpuid if -b was given, fills full paths, forces fixups for plugin files, runs process_checks, optionally generates the aliases, __symbols__ and __fixups__ trees and sorts. It opens the output (stdout for "-", otherwise fopen "wb", die on failure) and writes it with dt_to_source for dts, dt_to_yaml for yaml (only if built without NO_YAML, and only with dts input), dt_to_blob for dtb, or dt_to_asm for asm. For the output format "null" it writes nothing and still exits 0; an unknown format dies. Output file is not explicitly closed.
note: slice cut the head; real function dtc.c:164-380. Reviewer right: outform "null" does nothing (line 373-374) yet the run still exits 0. Not read: util_* and die implementations.

name: fdt_add_mem_rsv
prose: Precondition: fdt points to a flattened device tree blob; address and size describe a memory reservation. Postcondition: returns 0 after appending a reserve entry (address and size stored in big-endian form) as the new last entry, in front of the terminating zero entry; otherwise returns a negative libfdt error and the entry is not written. First FDT_RW_PROBE(fdt) runs fdt_rw_probe_ and returns its error if nonzero (this is skipped when VALID_DTB is assumed); the probe can return the errors from the read-only probe, -FDT_ERR_BADVERSION for a version below 17 (when LATEST is not assumed), or -FDT_ERR_BADLAYOUT, and when the blob's version is above 17 (and LATEST is not assumed) it rewrites the version field to 17 before returning success. It then calls fdt_splice_mem_rsv_(fdt, entry at index fdt_num_mem_rsv(fdt), 0, 1), which moves the later data up by one entry or fails with -FDT_ERR_BADOFFSET or -FDT_ERR_NOSPACE (no space) and, on success, adds the entry size to the struct and strings offsets in the header; any such error is returned. When the splice fails the blob may already have been modified by the probe's version change to 17, so it is not guaranteed to be unmodified.
note: fdt_rw.c:157-172. Reviewer right (probe can set version 17 at fdt_rw.c:36-37 before the splice can fail).

name: dialog_inputbox
prose: Precondition: title, prompt, height, width describe the dialog; init is an optional initial string. Postcondition: edits the global buffer dialog_input_result and returns an int. It copies init (truncated to sizeof(dialog_input_result) - 1 and terminated) into the buffer, or empties it if init is NULL. It returns -ERRDISPLAYTOOSMALL if the screen is smaller than the dialog allows (checked again after each resize). It then draws the dialog with an input field and OK/Help buttons and loops reading keys until key == KEY_ESC. While the input field is selected (button == -1): TAB, KEY_UP and KEY_DOWN fall to the button-cycling code; backspace, ^H and 127 delete the char before the cursor; KEY_LEFT and KEY_RIGHT move the cursor; any other printable key below 0x100 (including 'O', 'H', 'X', 'o', 'h', 'x' and space) is inserted into the text if len < MAX_LEN, otherwise the terminal flashes; these handled keys loop again without reaching the button switch. Non-printable keys that are not handled above (for example newline, KEY_ESC, KEY_RESIZE) fall through to the button switch. In the button switch: 'O' or 'o' returns 0, 'H' or 'h' returns 1, KEY_UP/KEY_LEFT and TAB/KEY_DOWN/KEY_RIGHT cycle the selection among the input field, OK and Help, space or newline returns 0 when the input field is selected and the button index (0 or 1) otherwise, 'X' or 'x' sets key to KEY_ESC and ends the loop, KEY_ESC calls on_key_esc(dialog) to set key, and KEY_RESIZE deletes the window and redraws from do_resize. Each return other than the too-small error deletes the dialog window first. After the loop it deletes the window and returns KEY_ESC. Because printable keys are consumed as text while the input field is selected, the letter keys 'O', 'H', 'X' and space act as commands only after a button has been selected.
note: inputbox.c:31-291. Reviewer right (printable keys incl. O/H/X/space are inserted as text when button == -1, lines 187-220).

name: dialog_menu
prose: Precondition: title and prompt are the dialog texts, selected is the item data pointer to highlight initially (may be NULL), s_scroll points to the saved scroll offset. Returns an int: -ERRDISPLAYTOOSMALL if the screen is under MENUBOX_HEIGHT_MIN or MENUBOX_WIDTH_MIN (also checked after a resize); otherwise a value chosen by the key that ends the loop. It sizes the dialog from the screen, picks the initial choice from the item whose data equals selected, uses *s_scroll if it is consistent with the visible window (otherwise scroll 0, and re-centres when choice is outside the window), draws the items, arrows and buttons, and loops reading keys until key == KEY_ESC. Keys are lowercased if alphabetic. If the key is not one of "ynmh " it searches the visible items for one whose first letter (skipping YyNnMmHh) matches the key, starting after the current choice and wrapping. When item_count() is nonzero and a match was found, or the key is KEY_UP, KEY_DOWN, '-', '+', KEY_PPAGE or KEY_NPAGE, it moves the highlight or scrolls and waits for another key. Otherwise the key goes to a switch: KEY_LEFT, TAB and KEY_RIGHT cycle the selected button within 0..4; ' ', 's', 'y', 'n', 'm', '/', 'h', '?', 'z' and newline store scroll in *s_scroll, delete the windows, select the highlighted item (item_set_selected(1)) and return 2 for 'h' or '?', 5 for 's' or 'y', 6 for 'n', 7 for 'm', 8 for space, 9 for '/', 10 for 'z', and the current button index for newline; 'e' and 'x' set key to KEY_ESC; KEY_ESC calls on_key_esc(menu); KEY_RESIZE deletes the windows and redraws. Other keys are ignored. After the loop it deletes the windows and returns key (KEY_ESC).
note: slice cut the head; real function menubox.c:163-416. Reviewer right: unrecognized keys are ignored (loop simply continues), they do not update highlight/scroll/button state.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the offsets generator in devicetable-offsets.c; takes no arguments. Its body is a sequence of DEVID(type) and DEVID_FIELD(type, field) invocations, each expanding to a DEFINE() from linux/kbuild.h that emits SIZE_<type> (sizeof the struct) or OFF_<type>_<field> (offsetof the field) as an assembler marker for the listed device-id structures (usb_device_id, hid_device_id, ... down to coreboot_device_id, whose last entry is tag). It has no branches and its only return is return 0 at the end. The file is only compiled to assembly to read these markers, the code is not meant to be executed.
note: Listed as <unnamed> and dropped; the slice (devicetable-offsets.c:253-287) is the tail of main (lines 9-287), which is a real function, so fixed. DEFINE expansion taken from the macro's usage, kbuild.h not read.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the sign-file tool; argv holds options and the positional arguments. Options: -s raw signature, -p save the signature, -d sign only (also sets save), -k use key id (only when built without USE_PKCS7); any other option calls format(), which prints usage and exits with status 2. It requires 4 or 5 positional arguments (otherwise format()); with -s they are raw-sig file, hash algorithm, x509, module, otherwise hash algorithm, key, x509, module, with an optional destination. If a fifth argument differs from the module name it is the destination; otherwise the destination is "<module>.~signed~" (asprintf) and the original is replaced at the end. When built with USE_PKCS7 a hash algorithm other than "sha1" makes it print a message to stderr and exit(3) directly. It opens the module with BIO_new_file. Unless -s is given it reads the private key and X.509 certificate, looks up the digest and builds a detached CMS (or PKCS#7) signature over the module; with -p or -d it also writes that signature to "<module>.p7s", and with -d it frees the module BIO and returns 0 without writing the signed module. Otherwise it opens the destination for writing, copies the module into it, appends either the CMS/PKCS#7 data or the contents of the raw signature file, then appends a module_signature record (with sig_len in network order) and the magic marker, closes the destination and, if replacing in place, renames the destination over the module; the final return is 0. Most failures go through the ERR macro, which calls errx(1, ...) when the checked condition is true (exit status 1); the BIO_free calls on the module BIO, the .p7s BIO and the raw signature BIO are not checked, whereas BIO_free(bd) on the destination is checked.
note: slice cut the head; real function sign-file.c:220-410. Reviewer right: non-sha1 under USE_PKCS7 exits via fprintf/exit(3) (293-297) and the other BIO_free calls are unchecked (354, 358, 375, 395); BIO_free(bd) is checked at 403. Helpers (read_private_key, read_x509, drain_openssl_errors) not read in detail.

name: toonie_init
prose: Module init function taking no arguments. It allocates the global toonie with kzalloc and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. Otherwise it sets codec.name to "toonie" (strscpy), codec.owner to THIS_MODULE, codec.init to toonie_init_codec and codec.exit to toonie_exit_codec, and calls aoa_codec_register(&toonie->codec). If that returns nonzero it frees toonie (the global pointer is not reset to NULL) and returns -EINVAL, whatever error the registration gave; otherwise it returns 0.
note: toonie.c:122-140. Reviewer only mechanical (contract omits ENOMEM/EINVAL), right; contract left empty because the function uses a global.

name: pmf_set_notify
prose: Precondition: rt is the gpio_runtime, type selects the notification (AOA_NOTIFY_HEADPHONE, LINE_IN or LINE_OUT), notify and data are the new callback and its data (notify may be NULL to clear). Returns -EINVAL for any other type. Otherwise it holds the notification's mutex (guard) for the rest of the function and compares the current notify (old) with the new one. old and notify both NULL returns 0 with nothing changed. Both non-NULL returns 0 if old == notify and the stored data == data, otherwise -EBUSY, changing nothing. old set and notify NULL: unregisters and frees the stored pmf irq client and sets gpio_private to NULL, then stores notify (NULL) and data and returns 0. old NULL and notify set: allocates a pmf_irq_client (-ENOMEM on failure), fills data, handler and owner, calls pmf_register_irq_client with the node and the name for this type; on error it logs, frees the client and returns that error without storing notify; on success it saves the client in gpio_private, stores notify and data and returns 0. A new irq client is therefore allocated only when there was no previous notify and a non-NULL one is given.
note: gpio-pmf.c:128-198. Reviewer right: same notify/data returns 0 without allocating (lines 163-166).

name: FTR_GPIO(headphone, 0);
prose: Generated by the FTR_GPIO(headphone, 0) macro invocation in gpio-feature.c, which defines two static functions: the setter ftr_gpio_set_headphone(rt, on) and the getter ftr_gpio_get_headphone(rt). The getter returns 0 if rt is NULL, otherwise bit 0 of rt->implementation_private ((implementation_private >> 0) & 1); it reads the recorded state, not the hardware. The setter returns nothing: it does nothing if rt is NULL or if headphone_mute_gpio is negative; otherwise it reads the GPIO with pmac_call_feature(PMAC_FTR_READ_GPIO), keeps all bits except bit 0 and sets the low bits to 4 or 5 (SWITCH_GPIO with the muted state = !on and headphone_mute_gpio_activestate: with activestate 0 mute is written as 4 and unmute as 5, with a nonzero activestate the opposite), writes the value with PMAC_FTR_WRITE_GPIO (neither feature call's result is checked), and then sets or clears bit 0 of rt->implementation_private according to !!on.
note: listed name is the getter; the invocation is FTR_GPIO(headphone, 0) at gpio-feature.c:132-164. Reviewer right: the macro also defines the setter that writes the GPIO and updates implementation_private (lines 133-153).

name: FTR_GPIO(amp, 1);

The getter returns 0 if rt is NULL, otherwise bit 1 of rt->implementation_private ((implementation_private >> 1) & 1); it reads the recorded state, not the hardware. The setter returns nothing: it does nothing if rt is NULL or if amp_mute_gpio is negative; otherwise it reads the GPIO with pmac_call_feature(PMAC_FTR_READ_GPIO), keeps all bits except bit 0 and sets the low bits to 4 or 5 (SWITCH_GPIO with the muted state = !on and amp_mute_gpio_activestate: with activestate 0 mute is written as 4 and unmute as 5, with a nonzero activestate the opposite), writes the value with PMAC_FTR_WRITE_GPIO (neither feature call's result is checked), and then sets or clears bit 1 of rt->implementation_private according to !!on.

name: snd_ctl_led_reset
prose: Precondition: card_number indexes snd_ctl_led_card_valid and group indexes snd_ctl_leds (neither is range-checked here). Takes a card reference with snd_card_ref (released automatically when the function returns) and returns -ENXIO if that fails. Then, holding snd_ctl_led_mutex, returns -ENXIO if snd_ctl_led_card_valid[card_number] is false. Otherwise it walks the group's controls list; for each entry whose card is this card it clears group_to_access(group) from the underlying control's vd[index_offset].access, destroys the entry with snd_ctl_led_ctl_destroy and notes a change. After releasing the mutex, if anything was removed it calls snd_ctl_led_set_state(NULL, group_to_access(group), NULL, 0). It returns 0 on this path, including when no entry matched.
note: control_led.c:303-330. Reviewer mechanical claim (prose lists ENXIO but contract omits it) right; contract left empty.

name: snd_fasync_helper
prose: Precondition: fd, file and on as for fasync_helper; fasyncp points to the caller's snd_fasync pointer. If on is nonzero it allocates a snd_fasync with kzalloc and returns -ENOMEM on failure (before taking any lock and without calling fasync_helper). Then, holding snd_fasync_lock with interrupts disabled: if *fasyncp already exists the freshly allocated one (if any; kfree(NULL) when on is 0) is freed and the existing one is used; otherwise, if there is no new allocation (on is 0) it returns 0 without calling fasync_helper, else the new one is stored in *fasyncp. It sets fasync->on = on, and after releasing the lock returns the result of fasync_helper(fd, file, on, &fasync->fasync).
note: misc.c:122-146. Reviewer right: fasync_helper is not reached when allocation fails (line 130) nor when on is 0 and *fasyncp is NULL (line 140).

name: boundary_nearer
prose: Pure helper on integer boundary values with direction flags (negative, zero or positive each treated as -1, 0, 1). It computes the distance dmin = best - min and dmax = max - best with boundary_sub (which only writes its two out-parameters and returns 0) and returns boundary_lt(dmin, dmindir, dmax, dmaxdir), that is 1 if the distance from min to best is smaller than the distance from best to max, comparing with direction as tie breaker, otherwise 0. The distances are passed to boundary_lt as unsigned int, so a negative difference converts to a large unsigned value. It reads no global state, does no I/O and writes nothing outside its locals.
note: pcm_oss.c:350-359. Reviewer right that old contract omitted the no-I/O/no-write guarantees; contract left empty because of the unsigned conversions and overflow.

name: snd_pcm_oss_change_params_locked
prose: Precondition: substream has a runtime; the caller holds the OSS setup lock (this is the _locked variant). Returns 0 immediately, doing nothing, if runtime->oss.params is 0. Otherwise it allocates sw_params, params and sparams (-ENOMEM if any fails), builds the slave hardware parameters in sparams (periods integer and at least 2; access mask MMAP_INTERLEAVED if mmap_count is nonzero, else RW_INTERLEAVED plus RW_NONINTERLEAVED when not direct), and applies the rate (choose_rate), channels (hw_param_near) and a format. If snd_pcm_hw_param_mask for the access fails it returns -EINVAL (not the original error); choose_rate, hw_param_near and _snd_pcm_hw_param_set errors are propagated. For the format it uses the OSS format directly when direct, else snd_pcm_plug_slave_format; if that is invalid or not in the mask it takes the first format in the mask that has an OSS equivalent, else -EINVAL. For non-direct use it builds separate client params (RW_INTERLEAVED with the OSS format, channels and rate), else copies sparams. It computes the frame size, calls snd_pcm_oss_period_size, then sets period size (snd_pcm_plug_slave_size) and periods with hw_param_near, issues SNDRV_PCM_IOCTL_DROP (result ignored) and SNDRV_PCM_IOCTL_HW_PARAMS (error propagated), and with CONFIG_SND_PCM_OSS_PLUGINS clears plugins and, when not direct, adds the format plugins (and a plugin built with plugin_first, appended for playback and inserted for capture), propagating errors. It fills sw_params thresholds from runtime->oss.trigger, mmap_count, the stream direction and nosilence, and calls SNDRV_PCM_IOCTL_SW_PARAMS. It then stores the slave period count into runtime->oss.periods, derives the OSS period size via snd_pcm_plug_client_size (-EINVAL if negative), allocates the plugin buffer when plugin_first, computes period_bytes and buffer_bytes (-EINVAL if the buffer size is not positive), stores format, channels and rate from params, replaces runtime->oss.buffer with kvzalloc(period_bytes) (-ENOMEM on failure), clears oss.params, sets oss.prepare = 1 and buffer_used = 0, calls snd_pcm_runtime_buffer_set_silence (error propagated), sets period_frames and returns 0. On any nonzero err it calls snd_pcm_oss_release_buffers; sw_params, params and sparams are freed on every path after allocation.
note: slice cut the head; real function pcm_oss.c:846-1091. Reviewer right: snd_pcm_hw_param_mask failure is turned into -EINVAL (889). Not traced into the called helpers.

name: snd_pcm_plug_slave_format
prose: Static inline fallback in pcm_plugin.h used when OSS plugin support is not compiled in (the #else branch, line 145): it takes a format and a const struct snd_mask pointer, ignores the mask, and returns format unchanged. It has no other return and touches no state. When plugins are compiled in, the same name is only a declaration at line 112 of this header and the real definition lives elsewhere.
note: Previously dropped; the stub at pcm_plugin.h:145 is a real function body, so fixed. Note the stub's prototype uses int rather than snd_pcm_format_t.

name: note_on_event
prose: Precondition: dp is the OSS device info, dev the synth device, ch, note and vel are the OSS values, ev is the event to fill. Returns -ENXIO if snd_seq_oss_synth_info gives no info. Otherwise the result depends on info->arg.event_passing. SNDRV_SEQ_OSS_PROCESS_EVENTS: if the voice table is NULL or ch is outside 0..nr_voices-1, it passes a NOTEON through with set_note_event and returns its result; otherwise ch is sanitised with array_index_nospec and, if note is 255 and the stored note for that voice is non-negative, it picks KEYPRESS if the stored voice velocity is nonzero (volume change) or NOTEON if it is zero, stores vel as the new voice velocity, and returns set_note_event with the stored note and the vel parameter; any other note of 128 or more returns -EINVAL (this includes 255 when the stored note is negative); otherwise, if the note differs from a stored non-negative note it first emits NOTEOFF for the stored note (result ignored), then stores note and vel in the voice, and returns the NOTEON set_note_event result if vel is nonzero, or -EINVAL if vel is zero (state updated, no note-on). SNDRV_SEQ_OSS_PASS_EVENTS: returns the NOTEON set_note_event result. SNDRV_SEQ_OSS_PROCESS_KEYPRESS: returns the KEYPRESS set_note_event result with note - 128 when note is 128 or more, else the NOTEON result. Any other event_passing value returns -EINVAL.
note: seq_oss_event.c:275-329. Reviewer right: the choice between KEYPRESS and NOTEON uses the stored voice velocity info->ch[ch].vel (line 296), not the parameter vel; vel is only stored and passed on.

name: snd_seq_oss_readq_put_timestamp
prose: Precondition: q is the OSS read queue, curt the current time, seq_mode the OSS mode. Holding q->lock (irqsave), if curt differs from q->input_time it builds an event record: in SNDRV_SEQ_OSS_MODE_SYNTH an echo event with (curt << 8) | SEQ_WAIT, in SNDRV_SEQ_OSS_MODE_MUSIC a timing event EV_TIMING / TMR_WAIT_ABS with time curt; any other mode builds nothing and enqueues nothing. For the two modes it calls snd_seq_oss_readq_put_event_locked, which fails with -ENOMEM when the queue is full (qlen >= maxlen - 1); the local flag queued becomes true only if that call succeeded. It then sets q->input_time = curt regardless of whether the enqueue succeeded or the mode matched. After dropping the lock, if queued is set it wakes q->midi_sleep. The function returns 0 on every path; the queued flag only controls the wake-up.
note: seq_oss_readq.c:228-257. Reviewer WRONG: the function returns 0 unconditionally (line 256); queued is not returned. The returned value is 0 on every path.

name: ctrl14_ev_to_ump_midi2
prose: Precondition: event is a 14-bit control-change sequencer event, dest_port's midi2_bank[channel] holds the per-channel bank/RPN/NRPN state, data points to room for up to two UMP MIDI 2.0 messages, status is unused in the body. Returns the number of UMP messages written to data (0, 1 or 2), or whatever fill_rpn returns on the RPN/NRPN/data paths (0 or 1). With channel = control.channel & 0xf, index = param & 0x7f, msb and lsb the two 7-bit halves of value: UMP_CC_BANK_SELECT stores the bank msb then falls through to UMP_CC_BANK_SELECT_LSB, which sets bank_set, stores the lsb and returns 0 without writing a message. UMP_CC_RPN_MSB/LSB calls fill_rpn(cc, data, channel, true) first (flushing pending data as an RPN or NRPN message, if any), then stores the new rpn msb and lsb, sets rpn_set, and calls reset_rpn if both are 0x7f; it returns the fill_rpn value. UMP_CC_NRPN_MSB/LSB calls fill_rpn(..., true) first, then stores the nrpn msb and lsb and sets nrpn_set and returns the fill_rpn value. UMP_CC_DATA and UMP_CC_DATA_LSB set both the msb-set and lsb-set flags, store the data bytes and return fill_rpn(..., false); since both flags are set at that point, the 'incomplete data' skip inside fill_rpn does not apply on this path, but fill_rpn still returns 0 when neither an RPN nor an NRPN is selected. For every other index it writes a CC message with status UMP_MSG_STATUS_CC, channel and index; if param is below 0x20 it writes data[0] from msb and data[1] (index | 0x20) from lsb and returns 2, else it writes one message from lsb and returns 1.
note: seq_ump_convert.c:946-1005 with fill_rpn (803-832) and reset_rpn (793-800) read. Reviewer right: the DATA path sets both data flags before fill_rpn(false), so it never declines for incomplete data.

name: snd_ump_parse_endpoint
prose: Precondition: ump is a UMP endpoint. Returns -ENODEV if the rawmidi core info flags lack SNDRV_RAWMIDI_INFO_DUPLEX, and the (negative) error from ump_request_open if opening fails (no cleanup needed yet). It then sends stream requests in this order, each through ump_req_msg (which returns 0 or -ETIMEDOUT): endpoint info (a failure here jumps to error), device info, endpoint name (failures of these two are only logged), then calls ump_set_rawmidi_name(ump), then product ID and stream configuration requests (failures only logged), then choose_default_protocol, then create_block_from_fb_info for each of ump->info.num_blocks blocks (failures skipped with continue), then snd_ump_update_group_attrs. At the error label, which both paths reach, it sets ump->parsed = true, closes the request stream with ump_request_close, converts -ETIMEDOUT to -ENODEV and returns err. Because err is overwritten by each later step, on the normal path the returned value is the result of the last executed step: the stream-config request if there are no blocks, otherwise the last create_block_from_fb_info result; so a negative result from that last step is returned even though parsing continued. 0 is returned when that last step succeeded.
note: slice cut the head; real function ump.c:1070-1139. Reviewer right: ump_set_rawmidi_name is called (line 1106) before the product-ID and stream-config requests, not after.

name: do_convert_to_ump
prose: Precondition: cvt is the converter state (buf, len, cmd_bytes, in_sysex, bank[]), c is the next input byte, data has room for at least two u32 words. Returns the value described below and updates cvt as listed; it never fails with an error code. c == UMP_MIDI1_MSG_SYSEX_START sets in_sysex = 1 and len = 0 and returns 0. c == SYSEX_END returns 0 if not in a SysEx, otherwise returns cvt_legacy_sysex_to_ump(..., true) (it returns 8 in the code read). Bytes whose high nibble is 0xf: a byte with zero length in system_bytes returns 0 with no state change; a one-byte system message writes data[0] and returns 4 (without touching in_sysex); other system messages start buffering (buf[0] = c, len = 1, cmd_bytes set, in_sysex cleared) and return 0. Other status bytes (bit 7 set) start buffering with cmd_bytes from the table, clear in_sysex and return 0. A data byte during a SysEx is appended to buf and returns 0 until len reaches 6, then returns cvt_legacy_sysex_to_ump(..., false) (8). A data byte with len == 0 returns 0. Otherwise the byte is appended; while len < cmd_bytes it returns 0; when complete it sets len = 1 (running status) and returns cvt_legacy_system_to_ump (4) for a buffered system message, else cvt_legacy_cmd_to_ump: 4 for a MIDI 1.0 protocol message, 8 for a completed MIDI 2.0 channel-voice message, 0 for a skipped one (bank select, an incomplete RPN/NRPN data set, unsupported status), and 1 when fill_rpn flushes an RPN/NRPN message (fill_rpn returns 1, not a byte count, even though it fills a MIDI 2.0 message).
note: ump_convert.c:447-512 plus cvt_legacy_* (255-445) read. Reviewer WRONG this round: a flushed RPN/NRPN message makes fill_rpn return 1 (ump_convert.c:326) and cvt_legacy_cmd_to_ump returns that value (lines 385-418); earlier reviewers who said 1 is possible were right.

name: loopback_jiffies_timer_pos_update
prose: Precondition: cable is a loopback_cable and the caller holds cable->lock (the function takes no lock). Returns running = cable->running ^ cable->pause, a bitmask of the stream directions currently running, on every path. For each running direction it computes the jiffies elapsed since that stream's last_jiffies and advances last_jiffies to now. If neither stream has elapsed jiffies it returns running immediately. If the playback delta exceeds the capture delta, it advances only the playback position by the byte count for the difference (bytepos_delta then bytepos_finish) and sets the playback delta equal to the capture delta; if the capture delta is larger, it computes the byte count for the difference on the capture stream, clears that many bytes of the capture buffer (clear_capture_buf), advances the capture position and equalises the deltas. If the common delta is then zero it returns. Otherwise it computes byte counts count1 (playback) and count2 (capture) for the common delta; the stream whose count is larger leaves last_drift on the other: if count1 < count2 then dpcm_capt->last_drift = count2 - count1 and count1 = count2; if count1 > count2 then dpcm_play->last_drift = count1 - count2. It then copies count1 bytes from playback to capture (copy_play_buf), advances both buffer positions by count1 (modulo pcm_buffer_size) and returns running. bytepos_delta also updates irq_pos, consumes last_drift and may set period_update_pending.
note: slice cut the head; real function aloop.c:664-717. Reviewer right: last_drift is stored on the stream whose own byte count is larger (capture when count1 < count2, playback when count1 > count2 -- lines 706-711), not on the smaller one.

name: fcp_avc_transaction
prose: Precondition: command and command_size give the AV/C frame to send, response and response_size the reply buffer, response_match_bytes how many leading reply bytes must match. Returns the length of the response on success (t.response_size after completion), a negative error from snd_fw_transaction if sending fails, or -EIO after ERROR_RETRIES timeouts. It fills a local fcp_transaction (state STATE_PENDING), marks it deferrable when the first byte of the command (read at line 243) is 0x00 or 0x03, and adds it to the global transactions list under transactions_lock. In a loop it sends the command with snd_fw_transaction (a quadlet write when command_size is 4, a block write otherwise) to CSR_FCP_COMMAND; a negative result leaves the loop with that error. It waits up to FCP_TIMEOUT_MS for the state to leave STATE_PENDING. STATE_DEFERRED sets the state back to pending and waits again without resending; STATE_COMPLETE returns t.response_size; STATE_BUS_RESET sleeps ERROR_DELAY_MS and loops again (resending) without counting a try, and nothing in this function resets the state from STATE_BUS_RESET; any other state (timeout) increments tries and, once tries >= ERROR_RETRIES, logs an error and ends with -EIO, else loops and resends. On every exit the transaction is removed from the list under the lock.
note: slice cut the head; real function fcp.c:229-288. Reviewer WRONG: the code does inspect the first command byte (line 243: deferrable = first byte is 0x00 or 0x03).

name: snd_oxfw_add_spkr
prose: Precondition: oxfw is an initialised snd_oxfw with a card and AV/C unit, is_lacie selects the LaCie variant. Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative error. It devm-allocates a zeroed fw_spkr (-ENOMEM if that fails) and stores it in oxfw->spec at once. For LaCie it sets mixer_channels 1 with mute and volume feature block ids 0x01; otherwise 6 channels with mute id 0x01 and volume id 0x02. It then reads the volume minimum and maximum, the mute state and the current volume of each mixer channel (channel index first_ch + i, with first_ch 0 for one channel, else 1) with avc_audio_feature_volume / avc_audio_feature_mute, returning the first negative error. Finally it adds the two controls ("PCM Playback Switch" and "PCM Playback Volume") with snd_ctl_add(snd_ctl_new1(...)), returning the first negative result (the snd_ctl_new1 result is not checked here). After an error return after allocation, oxfw->spec still points at the devm allocation, which is released with the card device, and controls added before the error stay added.
note: Listed name spkr_init does not exist; slice (oxfw-spkr.c:273-320) is the tail of snd_oxfw_add_spkr (lines 251-320), so fixed under the real name.

name: snd_tscm_create_pcm_devices
prose: Precondition: tscm is a TASCAM device with an initialised, not yet registered card. It calls snd_pcm_new(tscm->card, tscm->card->driver, 0, 1, 1, &pcm) (device 0, one playback and one capture stream) and returns its negative error if that fails. Otherwise it sets pcm->private_data to tscm and pcm->nonatomic to true, names the PCM "<card shortname> PCM", installs playback_ops for the playback stream and capture_ops for the capture stream, sets up vmalloc-managed buffers for all streams with snd_pcm_set_managed_buffer_all and returns 0. It has no other return.
note: Listed name create_pcm does not exist; slice (tascam-pcm.c:262-275) is the tail of snd_tscm_create_pcm_devices (starts at line 235), so fixed under the real name.

name: cvt_from_vref_idx
prose: Pure helper converting a VREF index to a compact index: with vref_caps a bitmask of supported VREF modes and idx a VREF index, it scans bit positions 0 up to NUM_VREFS - 1, counting the set bits of vref_caps below position i; when i equals idx it returns that count. The bit at position idx itself is not tested. If idx is NUM_VREFS or larger the loop ends without a match and it returns 0. It reads no global state (other than the NUM_VREFS constant) and changes nothing.
note: generic.c:2799-2810. Reviewer right that the old contract omitted the no-state-change guarantee; contract left empty.
